title: Test CrewAI credential redaction by scanning trace JSON for a fake key and asserting the mock was called
answers: How do I write a test that proves a CrewAI trace does not contain my API key?
How are credential leak tests structured in the CrewAI autolog test file?
Test pattern for checking secrets are absent from MLflow traces
body:
Convention in tests/crewai/test_crewai_autolog.py: define a fake key constant (_FAKE_API_KEY) and build the LLM with it, then serialize the output (json.dumps with TraceJSONEncoder, or trace.to_json()) and assert the key string is absent.
Capture the patched completion call (for example patch("litellm.completion") as mock_completion) and assert mock_completion.assert_called() before checking the trace, so the test cannot pass without reaching the LLM path.
For span-level checks, collect set_attribute calls from a Mock span and assert on the attribute dict; for input checks call _construct_full_inputs directly.
See test_kickoff_trace_does_not_expose_llm_api_key for the end-to-end form.
applies: Tests added for CrewAI autologging credential handling in tests/crewai/.
says: Private API keys are visible in the agent execution trace logs.
Secret LLM provider credentials appear in plain text on the trace viewer.
Redact sensitive authentication tokens from recorded multi-agent workflow runs.
Span details in the activity history expose confidential service keys.
